entries.title: Final Fantasy VII
entries.notes: Disc 1-3 report. Default 1x resolution and the ReARMed core hold full speed; keep texture filtering off for the battle swirl.

entries.title: Gran Turismo 2
entries.notes: Stable at 1x. Use the NTSC disc for 60 fps; the PAL release runs at 50 fps and feels slower.

entries.title: Metal Gear Solid
entries.notes: Full speed with the ReARMed core. The VR missions disc uses the same settings.

entries.title: Super Mario 64
entries.notes: Most areas run at full speed with GLideN64 at 1x. The Bowser stages and the castle courtyard can dip briefly.

entries.title: GoldenEye 007
entries.notes: Single-player is close to full speed; four-player split-screen drops frames. Lower the render size before changing anything else.

entries.title: Perfect Dark
entries.notes: Requires the Expansion Pak setting; combat scenes with many NPCs are the worst case. The boost plan lowers the render size.

entries.title: Sonic Adventure
entries.notes: Set Cable Type to VGA; with the default TV mode the FMV can stall the emulator. Threaded rendering should stay on.

entries.title: Shenmue
entries.notes: Crowded harbor and Dobuita scenes dip below full speed. Threaded rendering and frame skipping help; the story scenes stay smooth.

entries.title: Crisis Core: Final Fantasy VII
entries.notes: Runs at the native 480x272 with JIT. Keep frameskip off for the DMV cutscenes; battles are the only place it dips.

entries.title: God of War: Chains of Olympus
entries.notes: One of the hardest PSP titles for the A133P. Native resolution with frameskip 1 is the usual compromise; audio can crackle during big fights.

entries.title: Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition
entries.notes: Traffic-heavy races are the stress case. Use the native resolution and enable auto frameskip; the menu and garage are fine.

entries.title: Mario Kart DS
entries.notes: Full speed in single-player and local multiplayer. Keep the screen layout at one screen if the frame rate matters more than the map.
